Since 2008, We Are All About
Korean Traditional Dance
mission.quote:
Dance is not movement.
It is story.
mission.body1: Based in New Jersey, Choomnoori Korean Traditional Dance Academy is a cultural arts education organization that carries the spirit and values of Korean traditional arts to the next generation.
mission.body2: Students learn more than technique. Through breath, emotion, etiquette, and focus, they discover self-expression and cultural identity through dance.
mission.body3: At Choomnoori, classes, performances, and cultural experiences are connected. Children learn patience through movement, confidence through the stage, and their roots through tradition.
mission.body4: Choomnoori serves as a bridge for Korean culture in American society, continuing a wide range of activities to preserve authentic Korean traditional arts and share their value with local communities.
mission.body5: For Korean communities in the United States, Choomnoori also offers comfort, vitality, and lasting memories through traditional culture.

about.hero.description1: Choomnoori is a cultural arts education organization carrying the spirit and values of Korean traditional arts to the next generation. Students are guided to express themselves and discover cultural identity through dance.
about.director.bio1: Director Eun Hee Ahn is a traditional Korean performing artist and educator specializing in Korean dance and percussion. After graduating from Dankook University with a degree in Dance, she performed professionally with the Samsung Dance Company and now leads KTDOC as founder and artistic director, connecting education, performance, and cultural outreach.

pages.calendar.title: Get academy events on your own device
pages.calendar.description: Subscribe once to our performances, events, and camps. When dates, times, or venues change, your Apple, Google, or Outlook calendar updates automatically.
pages.calendar.sub.guide.appleIos.title: iPhone · iPad (Apple Calendar)
pages.calendar.sub.guide.appleIos.body:
• Tap ‘Add to device calendar’ above to open the subscribe dialog. If it doesn’t open, use ‘Copy link’.
  • Go to Settings → Calendar → Accounts → Add Account → Other → Add Subscribed Calendar.
  • Paste the link and save.
pages.calendar.sub.guide.mac.title: Mac (Apple Calendar)
pages.calendar.sub.guide.mac.body:
• In Calendar, choose File → New Calendar Subscription.
  • Paste the link, subscribe, then pick an auto-refresh interval.
pages.calendar.sub.guide.google.title: Google Calendar
pages.calendar.sub.guide.google.body:
• Click ‘Add to Google Calendar’ (desktop recommended).
  • If it doesn’t open, go to Google Calendar → Other calendars + → From URL and paste the link.
  • Google may take up to 24 hours to refresh subscribed calendars.
pages.calendar.sub.guide.outlook.title: Outlook
pages.calendar.sub.guide.outlook.body:
• In Outlook Calendar, choose Add calendar → Subscribe from web.
  • Paste the link, name it, then import.
pages.calendar.sub.hint: Once subscribed, new performances, events, and camps — and any changes or cancellations — appear automatically. Timing depends on each calendar app’s refresh interval.

push.guide.title: About alerts
push.guide.whatP: They are short messages that appear on your phone screen for a moment. Think of them like a text from a friend arriving. They come even when this website isn't open, and even when your phone is locked.
push.guide.whatFree: They cost nothing, and you don't have to give us your phone number. They arrive over the internet, not as text messages.
push.guide.whenNote: We never send advertising. Only things you need to know.
push.guide.iosLede: On an iPhone, you must first add this site to your Home Screen as an app before alerts can arrive. That is Apple's rule. You only have to do it once.
push.guide.ios1: Open this website in Safari, then tap the button at the bottom centre that looks like a square with an arrow pointing up out of it.
push.guide.ios2: Scroll up the list and tap “Add to Home Screen”, then tap “Add”. A KTDOC icon appears on your Home Screen.
push.guide.ios3: Now open that new icon and tap “Turn on alerts”. (You must come in through the new icon, not through Safari.)
push.guide.ios4: When it asks whether to allow alerts, tap “Allow”. That's it.
push.guide.androidH: On an Android phone or a computer
push.guide.and2: A small box appears near the top of the screen asking whether to show notifications. Tap “Allow”. That's it.
push.guide.andNote: It only asks once. If you tapped “Block” by mistake, see “I'm not getting alerts” below.
push.guide.deviceH: Turn it on once on each device
push.guide.deviceP: Turning it on for your phone does not turn it on for your computer. Turn it on once on each device where you want alerts. For most people, a phone is enough.
push.guide.offP: You can turn them off at any time. Go to “My profile” in the left-hand menu and tap “Turn off alerts”. You turn them back on in the same place.
push.guide.trouble1: First, go to “My profile” and tap “Send me a test alert”. If that arrives, everything is set up properly.
push.guide.trouble2: On an iPhone, alerts won't arrive if you opened the site in Safari instead of the Home Screen icon. Please come in through the icon.
push.guide.trouble3: If you tapped “Block” by mistake — on iPhone go to Settings → Notifications → KTDOC; on Android or a computer, tap the lock at the left of the address bar → Notifications → Allow.
push.guide.trouble4: If your phone is on Do Not Disturb or silent, alerts arrive quietly. Swipe down to check your notification list.
push.guide.troubleTail: If it still doesn't work, please let the studio know. Nothing is lost — every alert also stays in “My alerts” in the left-hand menu.
